verdict.rationale: Airbyte ships its own fixed event-to-action behaviours: per-connection rules for handling source schema changes, dbt Cloud transformations that run immediately after syncs, and email or webhook notifications on important events. These are preset triggers, not a general user-defined rules engine, and cron schedules are recurring timers rather than event triggers, so they earn no credit here. Missing for 10: arbitrary user-defined event conditions and actions, a general rules/automation builder, and any independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: You can specify for each connection how Airbyte should handle any change of schema in the source.
By using the dbt Cloud integration, you can create and run dbt transformations immediately following syncs in Airbyte Cloud.
If you want Airbyte to notify you about important events, use its built-in notification system.
Airbyte can send notifications to an email address, webhook, or both.
